findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a documentation-only pull request in Forge merges default-branch changes before CI runs.
The new merge check returns `test-only=false`, but `.forge/review-tests.py:250–253` sets it back to `true` for a docs-only change when required tests exist. Forge has such a list in `.forge/always-tests.txt:1`. The workflow therefore starts one group, while `src/forge/fasttest.py:328–334` widens its selection to include incoming changes, leaving the original 45-minute timeout problem. The same override exists in `src/forge/templates/review-tests.py:109–112`.
findings.title: Not done: A pull request whose branch has merged the default branch in runs the normal test groups, not one.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Scale
Case: normal use - a pull request changes one independent test without merging the default branch.
The workflow checks out GitHub's merge result (`.github/workflows/forge.yml:27–29`; see also `tests/test_review_record_reuses_parent_tests.py:30–33`), but `.forge/review-tests.py:248` calls `test_files` with its default `HEAD`. Consequently, the new `rev-list` always finds GitHub's synthetic merge, even when the pull request branch contains no merge. The matrix at `.github/workflows/forge.yml:44–53` runs six jobs instead of one, repeating runner setup and test collection on every such pull request. The shipped template has the same issue at `src/forge/templates/review-tests.py:29`.
findings.title: Run one group for test-only pull requests without a branch merge

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a grouped pull request merges default-branch changes before CI selects its jobs.
The new test uses the old fork as `BASE_SHA`, sets `HEAD_SHA=HEAD`, and checks only the classifier output. It does not model GitHub's merge-result checkout or a docs-only change with required tests, so it passes with both group-selection failures described above. The new-client fixture also starts with one configured group (`tests/test_groups_pytest.py:142–146`), so it does not prove multi-group execution for that delivery path. The regression needs to check the selected workflow groups for the real checkout and required-test cases.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - this fix's pull request is checked against its Done-when item.
The supplied proof list is `missing`. It does not map the Done-when item to a branch test and its pull request check, so the required proof cannot be assessed from the list. The added test needs to be included in a complete proof mapping.
findings.title: Gate: proof list

why: Bug 1522. The one-group run widens its test selection to cover every change merged in from the default branch, which takes longer than the group's 45-minute limit.
